tagline: The FL Players league newsletter · est. 2008
headline: Issue One: Two Byes, Six Playoff Spots and a Kicker Debate
dek: The first FL Players Weekly. Inside: Colt's perfect week, a kicker as Mikey's top scorer, the division races that decide the byes, the Kicker File, the brother bowl on Thursday, and every manager's story so far.
lead:
Five weeks in, the league has drawn its own playoff line. The top six are all 3-2 or better and the bottom six are all 2-3 or worse. History says that line is stickier than it looks: in every season on record, teams at 3-2 after week 5 have made the playoffs 71% of the time, and teams at 2-3 only 36%.

Week 5 belonged to Colt, who set a perfect lineup and dropped 146.68 on a Scott team that scored 138.24 and lost anyway. James won the closest game of the week by 4.96 over T.J., Brett hung the biggest blowout of the week on the commissioner, and Mikey fell to 0-5 with his kicker as his top scorer.

managers.text: 4-1, first in the standings and first in points (619.94). He beat T.J. by 4.96 behind Bucky Irving (30.5) and Joe Burrow (24.6), and he did it with Matthew Stafford's 27.32 sitting on his bench. Three straight wins, above the median in four of five weeks, and 94% playoff odds. His 4-1 starts have produced a title (2017) and a lost final (2016), and the one time he started 5-0, in 2019, he won the whole thing.
managers.next: Week 6: Austin, a rematch of the 2016 final that Austin won. Austin leads the series 15-10, but James is a 68% favorite.
managers.outlook: Best title odds in the league, a top-two seed more often than not, and one of the easier schedules left.

managers.text: 4-1 with only the seventh-most points in the league (527.54), and he has not cracked 120 once. He has been above the median in four of five weeks, so the wins aren't flukes. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (20.3), Braelon Allen (18.1) and Tyler Warren (17.9) were plenty against Anthony, 118.70 to 89.20. Joey has started 4-1 three times before (2019, 2022, 2024). He made the playoffs every time and won it all in 2022.
managers.next: Week 6: the brother bowl. Joey has beaten Scott four straight times, but the model likes Scott, 63%.
managers.outlook: The schedule turns his way. He has faced the second-toughest slate so far and gets the easiest one left, which matters for a team that wins without big scores.

managers.text: Scott is the only manager who has been above the league median in all five weeks, and he is 3-2. This week he put up 138.24, the second-best score in the league, and ran straight into Colt's perfect lineup. Jahmyr Gibbs gave him 35.2, the top player of the week. David Montgomery gave him 1.1, about nine points under his average, in a game decided by 8.44. His three previous 3-2 starts all made the playoffs, and one of them (2015) ended with a title.
managers.next: Week 6: the brother bowl. Joey has won the last four, and Scott is a 63% favorite anyway.
managers.outlook: The model rates his weekly scoring in the top three, and he has the second-best title odds. The two losses look like bad timing more than a bad team.

managers.text: The 2025 champion opened with 167.82, still the high score of the season, and has cooled since. This week was 89.20 in a 29.50 loss to Joey, with Isaiah Likely (26.9) the only starter over 20. He is still 3-2 with the third-most points, and his last three 3-2 starts (2018, 2022, 2025) all made the playoffs. The last one is why he is the defending champ.
managers.next: Week 6: Colt. Anthony has won four straight in this series and is a 58% favorite.
managers.outlook: A top-three scoring team with an average schedule left. Another 167 would help. A few more 89s would not.

managers.text: Every starter right, nothing left on the bench, 146.68 points and the top score of the week. Puka Nacua (29.2), Jacoby Brissett (24.78) and Malik Nabers (23.6) did the heavy lifting against Scott. That is two straight wins after a 68.90 in week 2. Colt chirps every week. This week he backed it up.
managers.next: Week 6: Anthony, who has won the last four meetings. Colt is at 42%.
managers.outlook: Two out of three simulated seasons end with him in the playoffs. Keeping the lineup perfect is optional, but it helps.

managers.text: 3-2 with the 11th-most points in the league (489.76). One of his three wins came in a week he finished under the median, and week 5 was 77.40, the quietest score in the league, with Aaron Rodgers (22.0) doing most of the work in a 27.20 loss to Austin. He has started 3-2 twice before (2014, 2021) and missed the playoffs both times. The odds have him at 34%.
managers.next: Week 6: T.J., who leads the series 9-7 and has won the last two. Nase is at 42%.
managers.outlook: The toughest schedule left in the league and the second-lowest projected weekly score. That is how a 3-2 team ends up a long shot.

managers.text: Lost to James by 4.96 with Jayden Daniels scoring 32.26 on his bench and CeeDee Lamb scoring 1.9 in his lineup, about 21.5 under his average. Only the Lamb call flips it: Wan'Dale Robinson scored 8.3 on the bench. Daniels over Jared Goff (28.94) would have closed the gap to 1.64. Four finals, no title, and now 2-3. History isn't kind here: one playoff trip in five previous 2-3 starts, and that was 2010. The points say he's better than his record, fifth in the league in scoring with 48% playoff odds.
managers.next: Week 6: Nase. T.J. is a 58% favorite and has won the last two.
managers.outlook: The second-easiest schedule left, after one of the toughest so far. His lineup calls will decide it.

managers.text: Two straight wins after an 0-3 start, and he still left 33.10 points on the bench, the most in the league. Drake Maye scored 39.46 sitting down, the same Drake Maye he has drafted in two different seasons. He beat Mikey 109.26 to 77.84 anyway behind Mike Evans (22.8) and James Cook (22.3). Board duty is his this year.
managers.next: Week 6: Buckley, who leads the series 10-9. John is a 57% favorite.
managers.outlook: The model rates his weekly scoring sixth in the league, better than a 2-3 record. A top-four hardest schedule from here doesn't help.

managers.text: Brett handed the commissioner a 132.94 to 93.10 beating, the biggest blowout of the week at 39.84, with Jaylen Warren (33.8) leading the way. It snapped a three-game skid and got him to 2-3. In 2019 he was on the wrong end of the biggest week 5 score on record, 224.06 to 98.64 against James. This year he handed one out.
managers.next: Week 6: Mikey, whose best player last week was a kicker. Brett has won four straight in this series and is at 55%.
managers.outlook: A top-three hardest schedule left and a projection of about six wins.

managers.text: Two straight losses, under the median in four of five weeks, and a 39.84 point beating from Brett. Davante Adams (19.6) led a lineup that left 12.10 on the bench, with Blake Corum scoring 14.7 there. The only other time Buckley sat at 2-3 after five weeks was 2018, and he reached the final that year. The odds give him 20% to make the playoffs at all. SKOL anyway.
managers.next: Week 6: John. Buckley leads the series 10-9 but is at 43%.
managers.outlook: The second-hardest schedule left and about a one-in-five shot. He needs wins against the bottom half.

managers.text: Austin won 104.60 to 77.40 while scoring under the week's median of 113.98, the luckiest win of the week. Josh Allen (30.5) and Parker Washington (27.4) carried it. 2-3 is practically tradition for Austin: seven previous 2-3 starts, and two of them ended in the final, including the 2018 title. He has four titles, so nobody should count him out, even if the odds (23%) mostly do.
managers.next: Week 6: James, the man he beat in the 2016 final. Austin leads the series 15-10 but is at 32%.
managers.outlook: The projection says about six wins.

managers.text: 0-5, and his top scorer this week was his kicker, Ka'imi Fairbairn, with 14.0. Pat Freiermuth scored 19.0 on his bench in a 31.42 loss to John. Ten teams on record have started 0-5 in this league and none of them made the playoffs. The odds give Mikey 3%, and a 55% chance at last place. Week 4 was the heartbreaker, a 1.72 loss to Anthony, so the first win isn't far off.
managers.next: Week 6: Brett, who has won four straight in this series. Mikey is at 45%.
managers.outlook: He has faced the toughest schedule in the league so far, and it eases from here.

tags.t: Most points left on the bench

trends.title: Points are up
trends.text: The league is averaging 108.0 a team through five weeks, the most since 2021 (114.9). The weekly average has gone up every week since a 101.2 in week 2, and hit 111.0 in week 5.

trends.title: Records lie, a little
trends.text: Joey is 4-1 with the seventh-most points. Nase is 3-2 with the 11th-most. Scott has beaten the median every week and has two losses to show for it, and T.J. is fifth in points at 2-3.

trends.title: Everybody has one
trends.text: A five-weeks-in redraft of the top 24 players made the rounds this week, and every FL Players roster has at least one of them. T.J., Austin and John have three each: T.J. with Brock Bowers, CeeDee Lamb and Christian Watson; Austin with Ja'Marr Chase, Josh Allen and Parker Washington; John with James Cook, Tetairoa McMillan and Ashton Jeanty. The first pick was Jahmyr Gibbs, who is on bye for Scott this week. Parker Washington is wanted, too. On A Rock and a Hard Place, the podcast Austin does with Colt, Austin said offers for him came in from "five teams out of the 12." He kept him: "I like him too much." The show had named Washington one of its sleepers back in July.

history.title: Week 5, all time
history.text: The highest week 5 score on record is James's 224.06 against Brett in 2019, a 125.42 point margin. The closest week 5 game was Buckley over Colt in 2023, 116.48 to 116.14.

ahead: Game of the week: James and Austin, a Division 2 game and a rematch of the 2016 final. Also worth watching: the brother bowl, where Joey goes for five straight over his brother Scott (Joey leads the series 10-5), Anthony goes for five straight over Colt, and Brett gets Mikey, whose best player last week was a kicker. Brett would like that noted.

moves.intro: One trade and a busy waiver wire through five weeks. Here's how the moves have worked out.

items.title: The only trade of the season
items.text: Week 1: T.J. sent Travis Etienne and Garrett Wilson to Brett for CeeDee Lamb and J.K. Dobbins. Five weeks later T.J. has started 119.8 points from his side (Lamb 95.6 in five starts, Dobbins 24.2 in three) and Brett has started 88.3 from his (Wilson 70.9 in five, Etienne 17.4 in two, and zeros in weeks 4 and 5). Lamb's worst week, 1.9, came in a 4.96 point loss.
items.verdict: T.J. by about 31 started points. Wilson is the piece keeping it close.

items.title: Colt's QB off the street
items.text: Colt picked up Jacoby Brissett as a free agent and started him right away: 24.78 points, second-best on the roster, in the perfect lineup that beat Scott. Brenton Strange, another pickup that week, started and added 10.3.

items.title: James's insurance policy
items.text: James added Matthew Stafford and left him on the bench. Stafford scored 27.32, more than the 24.6 from Joe Burrow, who started. James won by 4.96 anyway.
items.verdict: A good problem to have, for now.

items.title: Right players, wrong spot
items.text: Colt added MarShawn Lloyd and dropped him the same week. Mikey grabbed him, and Lloyd scored 16.2 on Mikey's bench. Pat Freiermuth, Mikey's other pickup, scored 19.0 there too. That is 35.2 points from his two new players while his starters put up 77.84.
items.verdict: The moves were right. Start them.

items.title: Marvin Harrison changes hands
items.text: Anthony dropped Marvin Harrison for Tank Dell, and Austin picked Harrison up. Both scored 0.0 in week 5.

nfl.intro: The NFL had a week that runs straight through this league. Colt took the worst of it: two of his backfield and receiver pieces, Deebo Samuel and TreVeyon Henderson, are headed for time off. Austin's Marvin Harrison Jr. changed teams, and Nase's kicker lost his job.

items.headline: Texans complete trade with Cardinals for WR Marvin Harrison Jr.
items.note: Austin has the receiver in the deal. Harrison goes from Arizona to Houston, where Mikey has Nico Collins and Anthony has Tank Dell, so three FL Players rosters now share one passing game. On the Arizona side, Buckley's Trey McBride and Joey's Michael Wilson have one fewer mouth to feed.

items.headline: Rams releasing kicker Mevis after miscues in loss, sign Grupe from Jets
items.note: Nase needs a kicker. The Rams cut Harrison Mevis after his misses on Monday night, which makes this a wire move before Sunday, not a lineup decision.

features.label: The races
features.title: Two divisions, two byes
features.dek: The byes go to the division winners, not the two best records.

blocks.text: FL Players plays in two divisions, and it decides who rests in the first round of the playoffs. The two byes go to the two division winners. Last season Anthony won Division 1 at 8-6 and got a bye, while Brett went 9-5 and had to play wild-card weekend. The other four playoff spots go to the best records left, from either division.

Division 1 is the real race. Joey leads at 4-1, but Anthony has scored 81 more points, and the model makes Anthony the favorite to win it, 42% to 33%. T.J. and John are two games back at 2-3, and Mikey needs a lot to go right at 0-5.
Division 2 is James's to lose. He is 4-1 with the most points in the league and wins the division 56% of the time. Scott, at 3-2 with nearly the same points, is next at 30%. Colt is third at 10%.
Week 6 has two division games: James against Austin, and T.J. against Nase. Of the 54 regular-season games left, 22 are inside a division.
Chances come from 10,000 simulated finishes of the season after week 5. A tie for a division is broken on points in the model.

Kickers come up in the chat every year, so here's the data. The test: take both kickers out of a game's box score and see whether the other team would have won. Since 2014, that's happened in 65 of 1,164 games, about one in 18. The records before 2014 only have season totals, so they can't be checked.

blocks.text: 📊 Coming next week: what if we had a median game?

Kickers aren't the only rule change that comes up. Next week's issue looks at league median scoring: every week you play your opponent and the league median, so a big score always earns a win and a bad one always takes a loss. Here's a preview of what it would have done to this season.

Thursday night: Seattle at Denver

Seven FL Players rosters have someone playing in the opener, and the best of it is the brother bowl, Joey against Scott. Joey has Bo Nix and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Scott has the Seattle defense, which means Scott's defense spends Thursday night chasing Joey's quarterback. Denver also has Austin's Jaylen Waddle, T.J.'s J.K. Dobbins, John's RJ Harvey and Nase's Courtland Sutton, and Nase has the Broncos defense too. On Seattle's side, Nase's Emanuel Wilson leads the backfield again with Buckley's Zach Charbonnet held out until week 7, and Colt's kicker, Jason Myers, gets the first kick of the week.

The Seattle defense is one of the popular plays of the week, which is good news for Scott and not for the Denver crowd. Nix has been one of the shakiest starters in football, and Waddle has one good game in five and is one of the most-asked start or sit questions going. Lineups lock for those players at 7:15 Thursday.
